transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendes (Aperture Head of ML), Priya Nair (Platform Eng), James Lee (PM)

Summary: Quick hands-on demo of Redwood Console Evaluate and Optimize. Showed how to upload prompt sets, tag examples, configure regression alerts, and run A/B comparisons across model versions and quantization profiles. Customer asked about latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/private deployment needs, and audit logs for compliance.

00:00:05 Maya Chen (AE): All right, everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a 45 minute deep dive, then leave time for questions. I see Aperture on the line, hi Carlos, Priya, James.
00:00:18 Carlos Mendes (Customer): Hi Maya, thanks. We're excited; we've been seeing some drift in product search suggestions after the last model bump so curious how you'd surface regressions.
00:00:30 Liam O'Connor (SE): Cool, I'll start inside the Console. Quick note — forgive any audio glitches, my mic is a little echo-y today.
00:00:37 [screen share starts]
00:00:45 Liam O'Connor (SE): Here is the Evaluate tab — you can create a prompt set, upload csv or JSONL. We recommend including reference outputs for a subset of queries so you can compute exact/pass-fail and fuzzy metrics.
00:01:10 James Lee (Customer): When you say fuzzy metrics, do you mean embedding similarity or something like BLEU? We use semantic match more than token-level.
00:01:25 Liam O'Connor (SE): Right, for conversational recommender work we usually use embedding similarity (cosine) and a human-labeled pass/fail. The console hooks both — you can add a metric comparator and set thresholds, e.g., cosine > 0.78 or rouge-l > 0.5, or custom script.
00:01:49 Carlos Mendes (Customer): If we put thresholds in, how will we be alerted? Email, webhook?
:01:55 Priya Rao (CSM): We have regression alerts that push to Slack, webhook, or email. Also can tie alerts to a PagerDuty route in Dedicated customers.
00:02:05 Maya Chen (AE): Important to note: alerts are delta-based by default — you set a baseline run, then a new model run will fire if metric delta exceeds your threshold. Very handy for catching subtle regressions.
00:02:22 Priya Nair (Customer): How do we define baselines? We have seasonality; some queries behave differently during promotions.
00:02:33 Liam O'Connor (SE): You can create named baselines by date range, tag them, or run rolling baselines. The console can also group by metadata tags (e.g., 'holiday', 'mobile', 'category: home') and compute metrics per group.
00:02:50 [transcription note: "baseline" mis-typed as "base-line" in auto-caption]
00:03:05 James Lee (Customer): Can we compare two model versions side-by-side — A/B style, like 60/40 split?
00:03:12 Liam O'Connor (SE): Yes — the A/B compare flow creates two runs, you can sample traffic, or upload sets that emulate production traffic. The UI will show per-metric delta, bucketed by prompt tags.
00:03:40 Carlos Mendes (Customer): And what about cost impact? If we enable higher sampling or background evals will that blow up tokens?
00:03:50 Maya Chen (AE): Great Q. Optimize can suggest sampling rates and caching policies to minimize token costs. For example, with prefix caching you often reduce repeat token counts, and the console estimates token cost impact per-run.
00:04:10 Priya Nair (Customer): We run on-prem-like workloads; what are the private deployment constraints? KMS, VPC peering etc?
00:04:20 Maya Chen (AE): For Private deployments we support customer-managed VPCs, KMS/HSM integrations, and you keep control of key rotation. We also provide audit logs to S3 or your SIEM.
00:04:35 Carlos Mendes (Customer): Is audit logging at token-level? We need to ensure PII isn't retained.
00:04:42 Priya Rao (CSM): Logs are configurable — you can redact or disable full request bodies. Soc 2 controls and retention policies are configurable in the Private plan.
00:04:58 [transcription imperfection: "SOC 2" captured as "sok two" in one section]
00:05:12 Liam O'Connor (SE): Back to the Evaluate UI: here's creating a prompt set. I'll drag in a small csv of 500 queries — each row includes prompt, expected answer, tags like 'search', 'promo', 'mobile'.
00:05:35 Liam O'Connor (SE): After upload you can bulk-assign labels: pass/fail/uncertain. For active QA we suggest at least 200 labeled examples per important traffic bucket.
00:05:52 James Lee (Customer): How do reviewers tag partial credit? Our product team sometimes wants graded scores 0-3 not just pass/fail.
00:06:00 Liam O'Connor (SE): The system supports ordinal labels; you can map them to numeric metrics and compute averages. The compare view can show mean opinion score and changes over time.
00:06:20 Carlos Mendes (Customer): Any way to automate human review sampling? We have limited QA capacity.
00:06:28 Priya Rao (CSM): Yep — we have a review queue which can export tasks to your internal review UI or return samples via webhook to your labeling tool. You can also set automatic sampling policies — e.g., random 1% + top-k low-similarity.
00:06:45 [short cross-talk]
00:06:50 Maya Chen (AE): Quick demo of regression alerts — I'll trigger a synthetic run comparing v1.14 to v1.15.
00:07:02 [demo noise]
00:07:10 Liam O'Connor (SE): You can see the run produced per-query diffs. Here an example where cosine similarity dropped from 0.82 to 0.65 on a 'promo' bucket — alert raised because delta > 0.12 threshold.
00:07:35 Carlos Mendes (Customer): That looks useful. Can we get consolidated reports for execs? Like top 10 regressions by impact?
00:07:45 Liam O'Connor (SE): Yes, the report generator aggregates by impact (metric delta * query weight) and you can download PDF or CSV for your stakeholders.
00:07:58 James Lee (Customer): For A/B experiments, how do we track user-level metrics? e.g. conversion lift
00:08:08 Maya Chen (AE): You can import custom metrics and map them to queries. Our analytics supports join keys so you can map query ids to downstream events and plot lift. For Dedicated/private you can stream metrics to your internal warehouse.
00:08:25 Carlos Mendes (Customer): Do you support hooking evaluation into CI/CD so model pushes fail if regressions exist?
00:08:34 Liam O'Connor (SE): Absolutely — there's an API and GitHub Action example in the eval-harness. You can block merges or production rollouts based on alerts.
00:08:50 Priya Nair (Customer): About latency — we can't degrade P95 beyond 200ms for suggestions. If we enable more sampling that might change tail latency.
00:09:00 Maya Chen (AE): We surfaced latency per-run — you can set latency SLO checks as part of the evaluation. If a model variant increases P95 above threshold, it will fail the pipeline. Also consider running background low-priority evals on separate Dedicated pools to avoid affecting production.
00:09:24 Carlos Mendes (Customer): What about quantized variants? We saw a mild drop in quality when moving to 4-bit; can Redwood compare quantized vs fp16?
00:09:36 Liam O'Connor (SE): Yes, the A/B compare treats quantized variants as separate model variants. The console will show token-cost delta, latency delta, and quality delta side-by-side. We also provide suggested quantization profiles per workload.
00:09:55 [transcription note: "4-bit" heard as "for bit" once]
00:10:05 James Lee (Customer): How customizable are alert thresholds? Can we set per-bucket thresholds?
00:10:12 Liam O'Connor (SE): Per-bucket thresholds are supported. You can also set alerts to ignore small-volume buckets to reduce noise.
00:10:25 Maya Chen (AE): We're going to demo a small A/B run now with a 70/30 traffic split simulated.
00:10:32 [live demo]
00:11:10 Liam O'Connor (SE): Demo output — you can see per-metric visualization: mean score, median, percentile bands, and a waterfall of top regressions.
00:11:30 Carlos Mendes (Customer): One of our concerns is false positives from noisy metrics. What guardrails do you recommend?
00:11:40 Priya Rao (CSM): Use a tiered alerting strategy: first stage — detect on aggregated metrics, second stage — only escalate if regression persists across 3 runs or affects >X weighted traffic. Also tune the minimum sample size.
00:12:03 James Lee (Customer): Do you keep a history of all runs for audit? We need to show a timeline for compliance reviews.
00:12:10 Maya Chen (AE): Retention is configurable by plan; Dedicated and Private can keep full run history for longer, and you can export the raw artifacts to your storage.
00:12:25 Carlos Mendes (Customer): Could you run a quick mock using our sample prompt set? We uploaded a small zip earlier.
00:12:33 Maya Chen (AE): We didn't pull it in yet — if you can drop the file to the shared drive, Liam can import.
00:12:40 [file upload noise]
00:13:12 Liam O'Connor (SE): Got it — importing now; quick parsing step. It mapped tags ok though there were a couple mismatched columns, auto-mapper guessed column names.
00:13:35 [transcription: 'auto-mapper' spelled as 'auto mapper' in audio]
00:13:45 Liam O'Connor (SE): Import shows 512 rows. I'll run a quick baseline against v1.14 and compare to v1.15.
00:14:05 [processing beep]
00:14:28 Liam O'Connor (SE): Results coming through — aha, a cluster of regressions in 'search:mobile' bucket, mean similarity down 0.08, and latency unchanged.
00:14:45 Carlos Mendes (Customer): That's consistent with what we saw during the last release — good catch.
00:14:55 Priya Nair (Customer): Can we automate a rollback if A/B shows negative lift?
00:15:05 Liam O'Connor (SE): You can configure automatic rollback on Dedicated with policy actions, or a webhook to your deployment orchestrator to trigger a rollback. For Hosted we support canary and fallback policies.
00:15:22 Maya Chen (AE): Another feature: annotate queries and add notes for triage so PMs can decide severity. Also you can assign action items right in the UI.
00:15:35 James Lee (Customer): Nice. Any gotchas on data privacy — e.g. storing user queries?
00:15:42 Priya Rao (CSM): We support redaction rules, PII detectors, and token-level redaction. For strict regulatory cases we recommend Private with no request retention.
00:15:58 Carlos Mendes (Customer): Pricing — what's the incremental cost to run these eval jobs?
00:16:10 Maya Chen (AE): Pricing depends on sample size and whether you run on-hosted or Dedicated pools. We'll send a POC pricing sheet with examples — e.g., 1k eval queries across two model variants is typically small compared to production token costs but we'll show exact estimates.
00:16:30 [discussion about contracts briefly]
00:16:45 James Lee (Customer): Who do we loop in for security review?
00:16:51 Maya Chen (AE): Our security lead is Ana Patel; Priya Rao will coordinate the SOC2/ISO artifacts and set up a security Q&A with your security team.
00:17:05 Priya Rao (CSM): I'll send the security pack and invite legal/security to the follow-up.
00:17:20 [short pause]
00:17:30 Carlos Mendes (Customer): For the POC, we'd like to test: a) regression detection on 500-1k queries b) A/B experiment measuring conversion lift c) a rollback flow. Timeline: 2-3 weeks.
00:17:48 Maya Chen (AE): Sounds feasible. We'll return a POC plan and timeline in an email.
00:17:55 Liam O'Connor (SE): I'll attach the eval-harness and an example GitHub Action to block deployments.
00:18:10 James Lee (Customer): Great. One last question — how do you handle model variant labels? We often have internal model tags like 'm512-v2-q4' etc.
00:18:20 Liam O'Connor (SE): You can import variant metadata; console recognizes tags and shows them in comparisons. We'll also preserve quantization flags and hardware hints.
00:18:35 [wrap-up]
00:18:40 Maya Chen (AE): Recap: we'll send POC pricing, eval-harness + sample prompt set, and schedule a security Q&A. Action items are in the calendar invite. Any final Qs?
00:18:52 Carlos Mendes (Customer): No, that's it. Thanks for the demo.
00:18:56 Priya Nair (Customer): Thanks — we'll upload additional data by end of day tomorrow.
00:19:05 Maya Chen (AE): Thanks everyone, talk soon.
00:19:12 [meeting ends]

Notes: transcript includes auto-caption artifacts and occasional mis-attributions. The actual call ran ~52 minutes; timestamps are indicative. Shared artifacts: link to eval-harness repo (internal), POC pricing deck (will be emailed), sample prompt set uploaded to shared drive.
